title: Play a turn of Operation: tweezer the Funny Bone out of Cavity Sam without a buzz and lay it on its card
instruction: Take the Funny Bone out of Cavity Sam with the game's tweezers without getting buzzed, lay it on its ailment card, and put the tweezers down.
context: Operation is a family board game nearly everyone has played. The rules (Hasbro, Classic Operation B2176): "Use the tweezers to remove the ailment without touching the metal sides." "If you touch the metal sides, you'll get buzzed, and Cavity Sam's nose will light up!" The tweezers and the metal edge are a battery circuit, so the game itself judges the hand. The gripper must hold light sprung tweezers and work them through its fingers: squeeze to shut the tips, ease off so their spring opens them to about 9 mm, no wider. The opening is only 3.5 mm wider than the bone all round and each tip is 1 mm thick, so the open tips clear the steel by about 0.9 mm a side: they must come straight down 65 mm below the fingers, centred to a millimetre, pinch the 2 g bone across its 6 mm shaft and lift it straight out. Fingers do not fit the opening, and a tip 2.5 mm off centre touches the edge. One arm does it.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left; heights above the table. (1) Classic Operation game board (Hasbro B2176), 25.1 x 40.0 x 4.1 cm, 0.45 kg, taped to the table, x 11.95 to 37.05, y -18.0 to 22.0; Cavity Sam lies along y, head at +y, nose at (24.5, 17.0). (2) The Funny Bone's opening at (16.5, -0.5), long axis along y: the bone's outline grown 3.5 mm all round (39 mm long, 13 mm wide at the shaft, 20 mm at the ends), edged by a 3 mm steel band flush with the top, over a 6.5 mm deep plastic pocket. (3) Funny Bone, loose, white plastic, 2 g: 33 mm long, 6 mm shaft, 13 mm across its knuckle ends, 5 mm thick, flat in the pocket. (4) The game's tweezers, steel, 14 g, 11.0 cm long, arms 1 mm thick, 7 to 3 mm wide, tips 12 mm apart (inside) when free, 1.2 N per tip to shut; standing tips down, arms apart along x, in a pine tweezer stand (5.0 x 4.0 x 3.5 cm, 45 g, loose) at (15.5, -23.5), slot 22 x 9 mm, 30 mm deep; their top 11.6 cm up. (5) Funny Bone ailment card, 8.8 x 6.3 cm, loose, face up at (29.0, -23.5). Arms at the ready pose. The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot.
scoring: Read every control step. The game's rule: a buzz during the removal loses the turn. A buzz: either tweezer arm touches the steel band with 0.05 N or more (PhysX contact force); the nose lights while it lasts. The bone is clear of the opening once its middle leaves the opening's outline or its lowest point rises 2 mm above the board's top. 0 for the rest of the run: a buzz while the bone is not clear (still in the opening or being lifted through it); a touch after it is clear does not count. At the end: 0 if the bone is back in its pocket or never out (middle inside the outline, lowest point below the top). 1.0 (success, held 1 s): the bone lies on its card (middle over the card, lowest point within 3 mm of its top), the tweezers are put down (every finger point 15 mm or more from them), and tweezers and bone are still (under 1 mm in 1 s). 0.3: the bone is out without a buzz but the turn is unfinished (on the board or table, in the tweezers, or the tweezers still held). Real trial: the game's own buzzer and nose light on the video (audio on); the card and the tweezers from the final frame.
reset_notes: Put the Funny Bone back flat in its pocket, stand the tweezers tips down in the stand's slot with their arms apart along x, lay the card face up on its tape marks, check the buzzer sounds when the tweezers touch the edge (fresh batteries). Simulation: each trial starts the simulator afresh.
fidelity: Rigid bodies, 20 Hz control. Board and cavity sizes from retail dimensions and photos (estimates). The tweezers are three rigid parts: two arms on hinges at the joined end, each with a 2 N m/rad spring (estimate); the wire to the board is not modelled. The circuit is the contact force between the arms and the steel band (0.05 N threshold); the buzz is counted, not sounded. The steel band is 1 mm thick (the real edge is thinner). The board is fixed.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (both arms stayed folded back near their bases, wrist cameras on the board; neither reached the tweezers and the bone stayed in Sam); demo: 1.0
